Comment: Thor graph-load workflow: writes one scan's changes into Neptune, once per scan. Started by the scan-completion gate as graph-load-{scanId} once every manifest of the scan has finished ingestion. StartRun lists what the scan changed from Postgres and hands back wave zero; a Distributed Map writes each wave's chunks as batched mergeV/mergeE upserts, every vertex wave before any edge wave; Finalize removes what the scan soft-deleted. Its end - success or failure - is an execution event the scan-completion gate watches: once the load succeeded and ATRE and Ownership are done, the gate starts PAI. Terraform substitutes the placeholders with templatefile; validate edits with: aws stepfunctions validate-state-machine-definition.

StartRun.Comment: Opens the scan's graph-load row, lists from Postgres everything the scan's successfully ingested manifests changed - and every endpoint of a changed edge - as files of ids, writes the plan to S3 and hands back wave zero.

MoreWaves.Comment: The loop. HasMore is true while the wave carries chunks. Every vertex wave comes before every edge wave, because mergeE needs both endpoints to exist and a wave is the only barrier here. Each turn costs a handful of history events against the 25,000 cap - a scan approaching it wants bigger chunks, not a deeper loop.

WriteWave.Label: WriteWave
WriteWave.Comment: One item per file of ids; each invocation reads its rows from Postgres and writes them as batched mergeV/mergeE upserts. Items arrive complete from StartRun and NextWave, so there is no ItemSelector. MaxConcurrency times each chunk's own parallelism is this scan's share of the Neptune writer - every tenant's scans write at once instead of queueing behind each other - and each body holds one tenant database connection. No failure is tolerated: a lost vertex chunk would fail every edge chunk that touches it. Upserts are idempotent by id, so the retry - and a redrive of a failed execution - rewrites safely.

NextWave.Comment: Reads the plan and hands back the next wave, or an empty one once every chunk is written.

Finalize.Comment: Removes from the graph what the scan soft-deleted - only now, once every write succeeded - and closes the scan's graph-load row.

RecordFailure.Comment: Closes the scan's graph-load row as failed - the one place that sees a chunk killed by its timeout. No DLQ: the gate started this run once, a failed one is redriven, and the row records why. The gate holds PAI back while this row says failed.

Catch.Comment: Failing to record the failure must not swallow it; the execution still ends failed with the original error in its history.

WorkflowFailed.Cause: See the scan's graph-load workflow row for the error. Every write is an idempotent upsert, so redriving this execution resumes it safely.
